messages:
claire.h: FYI I'm seeing TLS failures when using the Python SDK against our Dedicated private endpoint behind an outbound HTTP proxy. works without proxy but fails with error: 'certificate verify failed'.
mateo: Can you paste the exact error and how you're configuring the SDK?
claire.h: Error from app: `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate`
claire.h: Setup: REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://redwood-internal.corp:443, HTTP_PROXY=http://10.0.0.5:3128, and I set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/pki/my-org/ca-chain.pem
jin: Which client are you using sync requests or async (aiohttp)?
claire.h: We're on the async client via redwood.async_client.AsyncClient (py SDK 0.12.3).
ravi: This smells like the proxy connection doing TLS termination and the SDK not passing the custom CA into the proxy tunnel SSL context. I hit something similar with aiohttp where `trust_env=True` and `ssl` handling interact poorly.
mateo: Can you repro with curl to validate the CA bundle first? `curl --proxy http://10.0.0.5:3128 --cacert /etc/pki/my-org/ca-chain.pem https://redwood-internal.corp/`
claire.h: Curl with --cacert succeeds. So CA bundle is valid.
jin: Two hypotheses: 1) the SDK ignores REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE for the async client (different codepath), 2) the SDK is constructing an ssl.SSLContext but not loading the provided cafile when a proxy is set.
mateo: If you can run a minimal repro, it helps. Example repro I use for aiohttp: ```python
import ssl, aiohttp, asyncio
ssl_ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='/etc/pki/my-org/ca-chain.pem')
async def main():
    conn = aiohttp.TCPConnector(ssl=ssl_ctx)
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession(connector=conn) as s:
        async with s.get('https://redwood-internal.corp', proxy='http://10.0.0.5:3128') as r:
            print(r.status)
asyncio.run(main())
```
claire.h: Thanks—if I adapt that, it works. So user-level ssl context fixes it.
ravi: That confirms the SDK isn't passing through the CA when proxy is used. Looks like a bug where the SDK only uses the default context without cafile when proxy env var is set.
mateo: Workaround for now: create SSLContext and pass into client: ```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
import ssl
ssl_ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='/etc/pki/my-org/ca-chain.pem')
client = AsyncClient(base_url='https://redwood-internal.corp', http_proxy='http://10.0.0.5:3128', ssl=ssl_ctx)
```
jin: SDK currently doesn't document `ssl=` kwarg on AsyncClient well (or at all). We should add example and make REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE / SSL_CERT_FILE honored by default.
claire.h: Also FYI the order of precedence is confusing: REDWOOD_BASE_URL vs passing base_url param vs environment. When I set a runtime base_url it sometimes gets ignored if I also have REDWOOD_HOSTNAME set in our infra scripts. Might be separate, but worth checking.
ravi: Agree. Action items: (1) add repro test for proxy+custom CA to the client CI, (2) ensure env SSL_CERT_FILE / REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE are respected for both sync and async clients, (3) document the explicit ssl_context override as workaround.
mateo: I'll file an issue and link the test case. Anyone want to volunteer a quick PR to patch the aiohttp connector creation to load cafile from env if provided?
jin: I can take the PR — small change inside AsyncTransport to pick up cert file from env and pass to ssl.create_default_context(cafile=path) when connector is built.
claire.h: Thanks! Also tagging this as a customer-facing DX bug — Dedicated onboarding docs should call this out (private CA + proxy). :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Created issue #5482 for "py-sdk: honor custom CA bundle when using proxy / async client" and linked this thread.
mateo: Great — leaving a quick note for support: when customers report CERT_VERIFY failures on Private endpoints behind proxies, ask for curl repro and suggest SSLContext override as immediate workaround.
